definition: The instructions a publication posts for anyone who wants to send work: what they publish, length limits, file format, how to send, and any rules on timing or fees.
forYou: Read them in full for every venue, every time, because they change and they override any general advice (including this glossary).

definition: The window of dates when a publication is open to new submissions. Outside it, the submission system may be closed or work may be deleted unread.
forYou: Note the opening and closing dates in your calendar, and avoid sending in the last hour, when systems are busiest.

definition: A policy of accepting and reading work all year, with no fixed reading period.
forYou: You can send whenever the piece is ready, but still check that the venue has not paused submissions for a backlog.

definition: A public invitation from a magazine, press, or anthology asking for work, often tied to a theme, an issue, or a deadline. You will also see it as a "call" or "open call".
forYou: Treat the call as the guidelines for that issue; a theme usually matters more than a general style guide.

definition: Sending the same piece to more than one publication at the same time, so several editors are considering it at once. Often shortened to "sim sub".
forYou: Only do it where every venue allows it, say so if asked, and withdraw the piece everywhere else the moment it is accepted.

definition: Having more than one submission waiting with the same publication at once, either by sending several separate submissions or by sending again before hearing back on the first.
forYou: Most magazines do not allow it outside contests; wait for a reply before sending that venue anything new.

definition: A short note that goes with a submission, giving the title, length, genre, a brief bio, and a thank you.
forYou: Keep it brief and accurate; editors judge the work, and the letter only needs to show you read their guidelines.

definition: A brief description of the writer, usually two to four sentences in the third person, mentioning a few publications, relevant background, or where you live.
forYou: Keep a short and a long version ready, and use whichever length the venue asks for.

definition: A one-page letter pitching a project before sending it: a book to a literary agent, or an article idea to a magazine editor.
forYou: Queries are for agents and nonfiction pitches; literary magazines asking for finished poems or stories want a cover letter instead.

definition: The conventional layout for a submission: a plain readable font, generous margins, page numbers, and your contact details or title on the first page, unless the venue asks for something else.
forYou: When guidelines are silent, use a clean standard format; when they are specific, follow them exactly.

definition: The length of a piece measured in words, the usual way prose length is stated in guidelines and contracts. Poetry is more often measured in lines or pages.
forYou: Use your word processor's count for the body text, round sensibly, and stay within the limit; a limit is a firm ceiling, not a target.

definition: A widely used online platform that many magazines, presses, contests, and grant programs use to receive submissions and collect fees. Writers create one free account to submit to any of them.
forYou: Your account shows the status of each submission, but the label can be vague, so rely on the venue's own response time rather than reading meaning into it.

definition: The collection of unsolicited submissions waiting to be read, as opposed to work an editor has asked for.
forYou: Nearly every published writer started in the slush. A clean, on-guideline submission already stands out from much of it.

definition: Work that has already appeared somewhere publicly. Many publications count personal blogs, public social media posts, and some workshop forums, not just magazines and books.
forYou: Check how each venue defines it before you share a piece online; if it counts as published, you can usually only offer it as a reprint.

definition: How long a publication says it usually takes to reply to a submission. It may be stated in guidelines or estimated from writers' reports.
forYou: Note the stated time when you send, and only follow up after it has clearly passed.

definition: A brief, polite message asking about a submission that has passed the publication's stated response time.
forYou: Wait until the window has passed, send one short note with the title and date sent, and then be patient again.

definition: A policy where a publication only replies to accepted work. If you hear nothing by the stated time, the piece was declined.
forYou: Mark the date it lapses in your tracker so you know when the piece is free to send elsewhere.

definition: A volunteer or staff reader who does the first pass through submissions and recommends which pieces the editors should see.
forYou: A first reader's "yes" usually means your piece moves up for further consideration, not that it has been accepted.

definition: A status meaning your piece has passed an early round and is still being considered, sometimes also called "shortlisted" or "in second round".
forYou: It is good news, but not an acceptance; leave other simultaneous submissions open unless the venue asks you to hold.

definition: A standard decline sent to most writers, with no comments about the specific piece.
forYou: It is the most common response and says almost nothing about quality; log it and send the piece to the next venue.

definition: A decline that includes comments written for your piece, however short.
forYou: Treat it as encouragement; editors rarely write personally unless the work came close. Note the editor's name for next time.

definition: An editor's offer to look again if you revise the piece along suggested lines. Often shortened to "R&R".
forYou: It is not an acceptance. Revise only if the changes feel right to you, and reply by the date they give.

definition: A publication's decision to publish your piece, usually followed by a contract or a written statement of terms.
forYou: Read the terms before agreeing, then withdraw the piece promptly everywhere else it is pending.

definition: Telling a publication you are taking your submission out of consideration, most often because it was accepted elsewhere.
forYou: Withdraw quickly and politely, using the method the venue prefers (often a button in the submission manager).

definition: The legal right to control copying and publication of your work. In Canada and most other countries, it belongs to you automatically from the moment the work is fixed in writing.
forYou: When you publish in a magazine you normally license certain rights for a time, not your copyright; be cautious of anything that asks you to assign it.

definition: The right to be the first to publish a piece in a periodical, such as a magazine or journal. After that first appearance, the piece can no longer be offered as unpublished.
forYou: Once you sell first rights, future sales of that piece are reprints, so choose your first venue with care.

definition: Short for First North American Serial Rights: the right to be the first to publish a piece in a periodical in North America (Canada and the United States). Rights for other regions stay with you.
forYou: You can still sell first rights in other regions, such as the United Kingdom, but many venues now ask for first world or first electronic rights instead.

definition: The right to publish a work in digital form, such as on a website, in an e-book, or in a digital edition of a magazine.
forYou: Check whether a website keeps your piece online indefinitely, and whether you may ask for it to be removed after the exclusive period.

definition: A period during which you agree not to publish the piece anywhere else, typically from acceptance until a few months to a year after publication.
forYou: Note when exclusivity ends in your tracker; that is when reprint or collection use becomes possible.

definition: Permission to publish a piece that has already appeared elsewhere. Sometimes called second serial rights.
forYou: Many reprint markets are happy to have previously published work, though they often pay less; always credit where the piece first appeared.

definition: An agreement where the publisher takes every right to the work, sometimes including copyright itself, leaving you unable to reuse it without permission.
forYou: Be very cautious; for creative work, ask whether a limited licence would suit them, and expect higher pay if they truly need all rights.

definition: The written agreement that sets out the rights you grant, payment, deadlines, and how the work can be used. Some magazines use a short email instead of a formal contract.
forYou: Read every clause before you sign, ask about anything unclear, and keep a copy with your records.

definition: The publisher pays you when they accept the piece or sign the contract, rather than waiting until it appears.
forYou: This is the most writer-friendly timing; if payment is on publication, note the expected date and follow up if it passes.

definition: The publisher pays you only when the piece actually appears, which can be months after acceptance.
forYou: Ask what happens if they never publish it, and look for a date by which rights return to you.

definition: The point at which rights you licensed return to you, either after a set time or because the publisher did not publish the work by an agreed date.
forYou: Look for a reversion clause before signing, so a piece is never stuck with a publication that stops operating.

definition: How much a publication pays, often stated per word for prose, per poem or per page for poetry, or as a flat fee.
forYou: Compare rates fairly by working out what a typical piece of yours would earn, and remember some venues pay only in copies.

definition: A free copy of the issue or book your work appears in, given to each contributor. Some publications offer only copies as payment.
forYou: Paying in copies is common for small journals; decide for yourself when exposure and a copy are worth first rights.

definition: A small charge some magazines ask for to consider a general submission, separate from any contest. Some offer free options or waivers.
forYou: Look for a free window or fee waiver first, and keep a running total of fees you pay each year.

definition: The charge to enter a contest or prize, which usually funds the prize, the judge, and administration.
forYou: Weigh the fee against the prize, the number of winners, and the publication's track record before entering.

definition: An arrangement that lets some writers submit or enter without paying, often for financial need or for writers from under-represented groups.
forYou: Ask or look for one if fees are a barrier; using a waiver will not count against your work.

definition: A competition in which entries are judged against each other, usually for a cash prize and publication, often with an entry fee.
forYou: Read the full rules, especially on eligibility, rights, and whether non-winning entries are free to send elsewhere.

definition: Sending more than one entry to the same contest, each usually with its own fee, when the rules allow it.
forYou: Only enter several pieces if the rules say so, and keep each entry anonymous if judging is blind.

definition: A process where judges read entries without knowing who wrote them. Also called anonymous judging.
forYou: Remove your name from the file, the file name, and any headers; a name in the wrong place can disqualify an entry.

definition: The first public selection of strong entries in a contest or prize, before the shortlist is chosen.
forYou: A longlisting is worth adding to your bio, with the prize name and year.

definition: The small group of finalists from which a contest or prize winner is chosen.
forYou: Being shortlisted is a real credit. Keep the piece's status clear in your tracker until the winner is announced.

definition: A recognition from the judges for entries that stood out but did not win a placing.
forYou: It counts as a credit in your bio, and some contests still publish or pay honourable mentions.

definition: The last date (and often time and time zone) when submissions or entries are accepted.
forYou: Convert the time zone to your own, and aim to send a day early in case of technical problems.

definition: A complete story told in very few words, most often defined as under 1,000, though some venues set the limit at 500, 1,500, or 2,000.
forYou: Go by each venue's own number, and treat a flash piece as a whole story, not a fragment.

definition: An extremely short story, usually counted in the low hundreds of words or fewer; some venues use 100 or 300 words as the limit.
forYou: Every word must earn its place. Check whether the title counts toward the limit.

definition: A story of exactly 100 words, a form especially popular in speculative fiction communities.
forYou: Exact means exact; count carefully, and check whether the title is included.

definition: A work of fiction usually somewhere between about 1,000 and 7,500 words, though magazines set their own limits.
forYou: Most literary magazines prefer stories under about 5,000 words, so longer stories have fewer homes; check limits first.

definition: A piece of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novella, roughly 7,500 to 17,500 words in widely used awards categories.
forYou: Fewer magazines take this length, so look for venues that list it specifically.

definition: A short novel, commonly around 17,500 to 40,000 words, published on its own or in a collection.
forYou: Look for novella contests and small presses with dedicated novella series.

definition: True writing that uses literary techniques such as scene, voice, and structure, including personal essay, memoir, and literary journalism.
forYou: Facts must be accurate; if you compress time or change names, many editors expect you to say so.

definition: An essay that borrows from poetry, using fragments, white space, repetition, or images in place of a straight narrative line.
forYou: Look for venues that name the form; some poetry and hybrid magazines are its best home.

definition: A poem written in sentences and paragraphs instead of lines, relying on rhythm, image, and compression.
forYou: Check whether a venue files prose poems under poetry or under flash, and submit them where they fit.

definition: Work that mixes forms or genres, such as poetry and essay, fiction and documents, or text and image.
forYou: Choose the category closest to how the piece reads, and mention its form briefly in your cover letter.

definition: A short collection, often around 15 to 40 pages of poetry or short prose, frequently published by small presses or through contests.
forYou: Many presses run chapbook contests; check whether poems published in magazines are welcome, which they usually are with credit.

definition: A book collecting work by many writers, usually around a theme, a genre, or a year's best.
forYou: Anthology calls often have short windows; note whether they want original work or reprints.

definition: An issue built around a topic, image, or idea chosen by the editors, usually announced in a call for submissions.
forYou: Send only work that connects clearly to the theme; a strong piece that ignores it is usually declined.

definition: Any online system a publication uses to receive and track submissions, whether a shared platform such as Submittable or a form the publication built itself.
forYou: Use the exact system the guidelines name; work sent another way, such as straight to an editor's email, is often not read.

definition: Work sent without an invitation from an editor, agent, or publisher. Some venues read unsolicited work, while others take only invited or agented work.
forYou: If the guidelines say "no unsolicited manuscripts", sending anyway will not help; watch for an open reading period instead.

definition: A short proposal for a piece you have not yet written in full, most common in journalism and nonfiction.
forYou: Lead with the idea, why it matters now, and why you are the one to write it; a pitch sells the angle, not your whole history.

definition: A set of standard declines that differ by how close the piece came, such as a version that invites you to send more work.
forYou: An invitation to submit again is a real signal; send new work in a later reading period.

definition: The right for a publisher to keep your piece available after its first appearance, usually on its website or in a digital back catalogue.
forYou: Indefinite archive rights can make later reprint offers harder; look for a clause that lets you ask for removal after a set period.

definition: A partial payment for commissioned work that the publisher decides not to run after all.
forYou: Most common in journalism and assigned nonfiction; if you are writing on assignment, ask whether there is a kill fee before you start.

definition: Permission you give a publisher to use your work in specific ways, for a set time, place, or format, while you keep the copyright.
forYou: Most magazine agreements are licences. Check what uses are covered, where, and for how long.

definition: The rules on who may enter and what work qualifies, such as where you live, your age or career stage, and whether the work must be unpublished.
forYou: Check eligibility before paying any fee; an ineligible entry is usually disqualified without a refund.

definition: An umbrella term for fiction with imagined or impossible elements, including science fiction, fantasy, horror, and related forms.
forYou: Genre magazines often have their own customs on rights, pay, and format; learn them alongside literary ones.

definition: A short nonfiction piece built on the writer's own experience, reflection, or argument.
forYou: Editors usually look for a clear insight, not only an account of what happened.
